scope_note: Examples are split into finite-constraint illustrations and explicit generated-model counterexamples.

a_same_label_swap_does_not_prove_indepen.observation: abc and bac are both positive after swapping a,b, yet parity couples a and b in one true block; ac is negative.

b_positive_only_nonidentifiability.kind: two explicit generated models with positive-only data

c_incomparable_maximally_fine_feasible_p.kind: finite constraint example; not claimed generated by one known true partition
c_incomparable_maximally_fine_feasible_p.observation: The two feasible partitions are incomparable and both are maximally fine among feasible k=2 partitions.

d_pairwise_merge_blind_spot.kind: finite constraint example only; not claimed generated by a known-k=2 target

base.note: Under fixed k=2 on abc no partition is feasible; the one-block merge is only a finite-constraint illustration.

e_sample_consistency_not_target_or_parti.kind: same generated models as the positive-only example
e_sample_consistency_not_target_or_parti.observation: The sample is consistent with both partitions and both global regular targets, which disagree off-sample.

f_negative_allocation_can_change_true_ta.kind: generated-model counterexample plus sample-consistent alternate local assignment
f_negative_allocation_can_change_true_ta.observation: The negative abab is rejected by the true a-component via projection aa, but a learner can also reject it through b by excluding unseen projection bb; both hypotheses fit the sample.

g_unique_sample_with_incomplete_complete.kind: generated-model counterexample; labels and graph witnesses use the complete target
g_unique_sample_with_incomplete_complete.why_graph_is_empty: The only positive words have length 2 and every adjacent swap partner is also positive. Rescue requires xy=epsilon to be positive, but epsilon is rejected; any longer rescued positive is outside the finite target.
g_unique_sample_with_incomplete_complete.observation: The complete-generator graph has r=3>k, while the labeled sample uniquely identifies the true k=2 partition.
